text.p: Mannesmann AG said on Friday its group sales in the first five months of 1997 rose 16 percent to 14.3 billion marks, and that earnings in the period improved further.
The automotive, telecommunications, and pipes and trading divisions contributed to the improvement, the company said in a statement distributed at its annual general meeting.
Mannesmann subsidiary Rexroth plans to boost its 25 percent stake in Japan's Uchida Hydraulics to a majority in early July, Mannesmann chief executive Joachim Funk said.
Mannesmann said incoming orders in the five-month period rose 14 percent to 16.9 billion marks.
The engineering division remained in the red due to seasonal accounting swings, but Mannesmann reaffirmed its forecast of further profit gains this year.
The company said its engineering and tubes and trading divisions would earn much more this year, while a small increase was foreseen for automotive.
Orders in engineering in the first five months of the year were steady, but sales were up 14 percent.
Automotive orders were also up 14 percent in the five months, while sales rose seven percent. Tubes and trading saw orders rise 23 percent and sales grow nine percent.
The telecommunications division will hold steady thanks to growth in the D2 network, offsetting start-up losses in other telecommunications activities.

Sales in the telecommunications division in the first five months of the year rose 64 percent from a year earlier to 2.4 billion marks. Sales at the D2 mobile phone network alone were up 38 percent, with 2.7 million subscribers.
The remainder of the gain in telecommunications sales was attributable to Mannesmann Arcor, the fixed network operated by Mannesmann and other partners together with Deutsche Bahn AG.
The company said its operating result as a whole would improve this year.

Last year, Mannesmann showed revenues from ordinary activities of 1.01 billion marks, up from 900 million the year before. Net profit was 603 million marks, down from 701 million marks, on sales of 34.7 billion marks, up from 32.0 billion marks.
The workforce grew to 126,100 at the end of May, up five percent, mainly due to Mannesmann Arcor.
In the medium term, the company aims to boost returns to 15 percent of gross operating assets from eight percent in 1996.
